### Loading overlay
Covers part of a page while it loads, so nothing inside takes input until the page clears it.

Component ID: `loading-overlay`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/loading-overlay.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/loading-overlay.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.15.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.15.0

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: A settings form that saves to a server takes a loading overlay while the request runs; a dashboard tile that refreshes in place while staying readable needs a loading indicator alone.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-25); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-25, `llm.md#loading-overlay`): A region the page marks aria-busy="true" shows a surface scrim and its loading indicator and is made inert until the attribute goes, with focus taken from the control inside it, keeps an inert state the author set, announces the start and the finish in a status region after it with i18n strings, returns focus to the control that had it, and stops following the attribute on destroy().

Web adaptation: The native inert attribute blocks pointer and keyboard input instead of script handlers. The page owns aria-busy, and the script follows it with a MutationObserver. Inert content leaves the accessibility tree, so the script adds a visually hidden role="status" region outside the region.

Known boundary: Input blocking, the author's inert state, the status region, focus return, the scrim and indicator geometry and destroy() are checked in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; spoken output from the status region and real forced-colors themes remain unverified. The scrim does not follow the content of a region that scrolls itself; the docs say to wrap the scroller.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#loading-overlay).

#### Contract

A `.loading-overlay` region holds a `.loading-indicator` as a direct child and the content. `AutoInit()` starts every `.loading-overlay`. The page sets `aria-busy="true"` on the region when its work starts, and removes the attribute, or sets any other value, when the work is done; there is no method for either. While the region is busy, a scrim covers it, the indicator shows in its centre, and the script makes the region `inert`, so nothing inside takes a click, a tap or keyboard focus. When it clears, the region gets back the `inert` state it had before.

#### Syntax

```html
<form class="loading-overlay">
  <span class="loading-indicator contained" role="status" aria-label="Saving"></span>
  <div class="field">
    <input id="name" type="text" placeholder=" ">
    <label for="name">Name</label>
  </div>
  <button type="submit" class="filled">Save</button>
</form>
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `i18n` | Object | `{ loading: 'Loading', loaded: 'Loaded' }` | What the status region announces when the region becomes busy and when it clears. |

#### Methods

- `.destroy()`: Stops following `aria-busy`, removes the status region, and gives the region back the `inert` state it had before. The scrim still follows the attribute, so remove `aria-busy` too if the region should look available.

#### Also documented

The Loading overlay section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `loading-overlay-has-an-indicator`: Give a .loading-overlay a .loading-indicator as a direct child. It is what shows over the scrim while the region is busy.
